title: Rabbinic Judaism after the Second Temple
summary: Rabbinic Judaism took shape between the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple in 70 CE and the Muslim conquest of the Near East about 640. It stressed a dual revelation to Moses of written and oral Torah, the leadership of the sage or rabbi, and doing God's will through Torah study. Its core documents are the Mishnah, about 200 CE, and two Talmuds, from the Land of Israel and Babylonia, the latter about 500.
